messages:
maya: heads up — starting bring-up for the new quantized 40B (q4f16) on Dedicated.
maya: plan is to test H100 and A100 across us-west and eu-west to get latency/throughput curves and then pick pool sizing + concurrency targets.
maya: curious on heuristics people use for autoscale headroom with mixed kernels (tiling on H100, fused on A100).
omar: basic numbers from quick runs — single H100 (p99 gen latency) at concurrency=8 ~ 220ms for 1k tokens; A100 at same concurrency ~ 270ms.
omar: throughput (tokens/s) H100 ≈ 950, A100 ≈ 760 on our quick config.
lina: double-check kernel mix: H100 run used tiled-attn kernel v2; A100 used fused-kernel fallback. that explains latency gap.
lina: quant profile q4f16 reduces memory but some kernels are slower due to extra dequant steps.
chris: for Dedicated sizing: aim for p99 SLO buffer of 1.5x observed p99 under baseline load.
chris: e.g., if target p99=300ms, and measured p99 at concurrency N is 200ms, plan headroom factor = 1.5 => provision for ~N*1.5 concurrency capacity.
chris: in practice we set per-GPU concurrency target (soft limit) to the concurrency where throughput starts to plateau — then autoscaler uses slot-based pods.
kai: autoscaler tip — use cooldown=60s and scale_delta=1 for steady traffic, but allow burst_policy with short slot-burst up to +30% for expected microbursts.
kai: also recommend target CPU for sidecar at 30% so metrics don't throttle kv cache ops during burst.
maya: can you paste the small run command + config you used? would like to replicate.
omar: sure — snippet:

```
run_bench --model 40b-q4f16 --gpu h100 --concurrency 8 --seq 1024 --region us-west --kernels tiled-v2
```

omar: autoscale config I tested:

```
autoscaler:
  mode: slot
  slot_size: 2
  cooldown_sec: 60
  burst_max_pct: 30
```

devbot: loadtest finished: us-west H100 concurrency sweep [4,8,12]
devbot: results summary: p50/p95/p99 tokens/s = [920/880/820] at c=8; p99 latency 220ms; memory headroom 18%.
devbot: eu-west A100 sweep: p50/p95/p99 tokens/s = [760/720/680] at c=8; p99 latency 270ms; memory headroom 22%.
lina: small caveat — eu-west runs had slightly higher tail due to AZ network jitter during the window.
chris: rough capacity calc: for sustained 10k tok/s traffic in us-west, with q4f16 on H100 at 920 tok/s -> need ceil(10000/920)=11 GPUs, then add 20% autoscale runway => 14 GPUs.
chris: for eu-west on A100 at 760 tok/s -> ceil(10000/760)=14 GPUs, +20% => 17 GPUs.
maya: good, that aligns with rough sims. want to translate to tenant-level concurrency targets — how do we map tokens/s to concurrency for routing?
omar: mapping: tokens/s per GPU = (throughput per request) * requests/s. if average request is 500 tokens, then requests/s = tok/s / 500.
omar: so with 920 tok/s, requests/s ≈ 1.84 => if avg latency ~0.22s, concurrency per GPU ≈ requests/s * latency ≈ 0.4. that seems low because of KV caching — better to measure requests-at-concurrency directly.
kai: operationally I recommend setting per-GPU soft_concurrency = 10 for 40B q4f16 on H100, and 8 on A100, then use loadtests to tune.
kai: also keep a warm-slab pool of 2-3 GPUs per AZ for cold-start smoothing.
maya: any kernel fallback strategy recommendations? want to avoid sudden p99 jumps if tiled kernel OOMs.
lina: set automatic fallback to nearest compatible kernel and trigger a slow-path alert if fallback rate > 1% in 5m window.
lina: eg alert rule: `fallback_rate > 0.01` -> notify eng-ml and autoscale to add +1 slot.
sre-bot: added runbook note: when fallback detected -> roll to previous kernel build, trigger canary on 1/10 traffic.
sre-bot: runbook excerpt: "If p99 increases > 30% after kernel change, revert and notify model-onboard oncall."
maya: next steps: I'll run full regional sweep with longer traffic tails (90m) and post charts (latency hist + throughput vs concurrency) here.
maya: tagging @kai for autoscaler configs and @lina for kernel flags — will share raw CSVs.
chris: quick ask — include cold-start tail in the sweep (simulate new sessions) and a steady-state run; both matter for Dedicated SLAs.
maya: yep, will do both. thanks all :rocket:
